metadata.title: ARM Holdings earnings analysis: questions answered and next catalysts

content.text:
Investing.com -- Arm Holdings ADR (ARM) beat on every headline number, and the stock fell anyway. The fiscal Q2 2027 report came out after the Nov 4 close. EPS was $0.52 vs $0.47 expected (+10.6%), and revenue was $1.44B vs $1.38B.
Arm Holdings ADR (ARM): Trading at $168.37, -12.22% on the day, as of Nov 5, 1:24 PM EST (Market Cap: $180.42B) || 1W: -26.43% || 1M: -44.43% || 52W range: $100.02–$452.70
The pre-open indication was only about -3.4%. The selling deepened once the market digested the royalty detail. The stock has now lost nearly half its value in a month, so expectations were elevated going in. Peers' disappointing handset numbers added to the pressure.
Questions Answered
-
Is licensing strong? Yes. Licensing revenue was $773M, up 50% YoY, helped by new ATA and CSS agreements. HSBC put it 16% above consensus.
-
Is the AGI CPU supply-constrained? Less so. Management secured more supply and expressed confidence in meeting up to $2B of customer demand. It also sees upside to its $1B+ revenue target, though it did not formally raise it.
-
Are data center royalties real? Yes. They doubled, according to RBC's read of the call.
Questions Left Open
-
Royalties lagged. They rose just 8% YoY to $670M, against Barclays' 14% estimate. Royalties track actual chip shipments, so they are the cleaner demand signal. Android weakness is the culprit.
-
Guidance was thin. Q3 revenue guidance of about $1.54B barely topped the $1.53B consensus.
-
Margins may be under pressure. Barclays flagged the AGI CPU hardware business and rising operating expenses. It cut its target to $325 from $360.
-
The Qualcomm licensing dispute is still unresolved.
Arm has now beaten four quarters running. Its price reactions have shifted from positive to negative.
Analyst Split
-
Bulls: Barclays $325, RBC $300 (Outperform), Piper Sandler $270, Needham $255, Wells Fargo $255. Most cut targets on sector multiple compression rather than on the business.
-
Skeptics: HSBC cut to $215 (Hold). Goldman Sachs reiterated Sell at $160, expecting the stock to stay range-bound.
-
RBC noted a trailing P/E near 195 and said InvestingPro analysis suggests the stock looks overvalued.
